description:
Step-by-step derivation of p (proton, A=1)'s archimedean Markov trace value tr_M(p, q_0) ≈ 2.12258250945273 from the seven first-principles entrypoints.  Per the methodology directive (post-#472), every numerical claim must trace back here.  SCRIPT_CITED steps are the computational frontier; each needs its own derivation chain to push back the frontier.

CONVENTION AND PIN SCOPING (2026-08-30, bean `qou-rm57`). This document is
DOUBLY off canon, and neither departure was declared:

  1. CONVENTION C. Its numbers use the Markov parameter z = sqrt(q)/(q+1).
     The owner ruling of 2026-08-15 makes convention D (z = q^3/(q^2+1))
     canonical. Live D value for this atom, at the canonical proton pin:
         tr_M(p) = 1.14575969245730086968908159577411930594372806194352738498820
     (source: computations/atomic-tr-m-mpfr-50dps-proton.witness.json, and
     derivation_chain.py::TR_M_AT_Q0, which therefore DISAGREES with the
     target_value above.)

  2. THE MUON PIN USED IS NEITHER LIVE ANCHOR. Step 7 evaluates at
     q_0 = 1.1099785955541805 — the CODATA-2018 lepton-tower derivation, not
     the frozen canonical muon pin (1.1099785955573347...) and not the proton
     pin the 2026-08-15 ruling makes default for compute.

     Established rather than assumed: the target differs from the exact
     convention-C proton trace at the FROZEN muon pin by rel 1.9504e-11,
     while dq/q between the two muon pins is 2.8417e-12 — an elasticity of
     6.86, which is exactly the scale a Laurent polynomial spanning q^-6..q^6
     gives (the proton braid word has 6 crossings; chi^(3) = q^6,
     chi^(111) = q^-6). Float64 truncation is REFUTED as the explanation: it
     would agree to ~1e-16, not diverge at the 11th digit.

The DERIVATION is not in question — the Hecke presentation, Wedderburn
decomposition, Schur-Weyl weights and Frobenius pairing are all
convention-independent. Only the evaluation carries the frame.

Kept as recorded, not corrected: the values are right for their own frame and
pin, and re-deriving under D at the proton pin is a compute, not an edit.

steps.name: Hecke algebra H_3(q) presentation
steps.operation: Define H_3(q) := ⟨σ_1..σ_2 | braid relations, Hecke relation (σ_i - q)(σ_i + q^{-1}) = 0⟩.
steps.notes: Hecke energy axiom: each σ_i carries σ_i^2 = (q-q^{-1})σ_i + 1; the (q-q^{-1}) factor is the per-crossing energy (AGENTS.md §7a).

steps.name: Wedderburn decomposition of H_3(q)
steps.operation: H_3(q) ≅ ⊕_{λ ⊢ 3} M_{f_λ}(K(q)) (semisimple at generic q, including q_0).
steps.notes: Partitions of 3 index the simple factors; Hoefsmit frame dimensions f_λ from `schur_weyl_symbolic.partitions_of`.  Mathlib backs the abstract direct-sum statement via `Algebra.Algebraic.Module.WedderburnArtin`.

steps.name: Schur–Weyl weights w_λ(q)
steps.operation: For each λ, compute w_λ(q) per Schur–Weyl duality U_q(sl_2) ↺ V^{⊗3A}; Hoefsmit normalisation (Kassel §III.4).
steps.notes: script: computations/schur_weyl_symbolic.py function `schur_weyl_weight(lam, q)`.  SCRIPT_CITED pending its own derivation chain.

steps.name: Categorical action B_3 → ⊕_λ M_{f_λ}
steps.operation: Categorical action of B_3 on V^{⊗3A} via the R-matrix; project to each λ-block to get ρ^λ : H → M_{f_λ}(K(q)).
steps.output_value: ρ^λ for each λ — see hecke_character_symbolic.py
steps.notes: script: computations/hecke/hecke_character_symbolic.py Hoefsmit-matrix evaluation of σ_i.  SCRIPT_CITED.

steps.name: Atomic p Hecke element T_w(Z=1, N=0) -- NOT a braid word
steps.operation: Atomic recipe: Z=1 up-strands, N=0 down-strands, include_inter=False. `atom_braid_word_3A` returns 11 triples (c, d, g) on 3 strands, each denoting the HECKE ELEMENT c*sigma_g + d*1 -- not a braid generator. Measured composition: 6 sigma (d = 0), 3 sigma^-1 (d = -h), and 2 weight-1 averages over crossing sign (2 colour-blind (-h/2)), the latter being 2A = 2 letters that lie OUTSIDE rho(B_3). So T_w is in H_3(q) but NOT in the image of rho, and it has no crossing number, no volume and no genus.
steps.output_value: T_w in H_3(q): 11 Hecke letters (6 sigma, 3 sigma^-1, 2 averaged) on 3 strands (Z=1, N=0, include_inter=False)
steps.notes: producer: computations/mass_at_3A_proper.py function `atom_braid_word_3A`; letter classification: computations/canonical_braid_crossings.py `classify_crossing`, reached via markov/markov_weights_symbolic.py `atom_braid_word_3A_to_crossings`. CORRECTED 2026-08-30 (bean qou-1ucq). This step previously read "produces a word with 6 crossings on 3 strands", which was wrong twice over. (i) There is no crossing number to report: `atom_braid_word_3A`'s own docstring (PR #5765) states that the object is a list of Hecke elements, that it is not in the image of rho, and that NO topological quantity -- volume, crossing number or genus -- may be read off it, because tr_M of it is by linearity a weighted sum of 2^(2A+1) link invariants rather than the invariant of one link. (ii) Even as a letter count the figure was wrong: the object has 11 letters, not 6. Measured across the three chains, the discarded figures did not even use one convention -- p's 6 and n's 5 are the sigma (d = 0) counts alone, while D's 12 is the complement (sigma^-1 plus averaged); no single rule yields all three. The value this chain reports is unaffected, because the character step below evaluates chi^lambda as a trace of the seminormal representation matrix and never consults a crossing count. SCRIPT_CITED -- the atomic recipe itself awaits formalisation.

steps.name: Frobenius pairing — characters χ^λ_q(T_w)
steps.operation: For each λ, compute χ^λ_q(T_w) := tr(ρ^λ(T_w)) (Frobenius pairing identifies traces with characters of the regular rep).
steps.output_value: χ^λ_q(T_w) Laurent polynomial in q for each λ ⊢ 3

steps.name: Markov trace via finite-Jones formula
steps.operation: tr_M(T_w, q) := Σ_{λ ⊢ 3} w_λ(q) · χ^λ_q(T_w); uniqueness from the Markov property + finite-Jones.
steps.output_value: symbolic Laurent polynomial in q (Markov trace)
steps.notes: Derivation chain: markov-trace-assembly-proton.derivation.json. Combines schur-weyl-weight-{3,21,111} + hoefsmit-rep-21-sigma1 (σ_2 covered by SYT-relabelling symmetry within the (2,1) block). The CANONICAL proton σ-word is derived in atomic-braid-recipe-p.derivation.json (11 letters = 6 σ + 3 σ^{-1} + 2 averaged; 9 lie in rho(B_3), the 2 averaged do not)  [letters, not crossings -- corrected 2026-09-04, bean `qou-1ucq`. Step 4 of this chain family states that the atomic element is a list of Hecke elements, is NOT in the image of rho, and therefore HAS NO CROSSING NUMBER; the 2026-08-30 pass corrected that step and left this one saying 'crossings'. The composition below is measured from `atom_braid_word_3A` at the production pin and is unchanged -- only the word is.].  The assembly chain's chi-step operations use a SEPARATE LEGACY 6-letter σ-word convention (T_w_p = σ_1 σ_2 σ_1 σ_2 σ_1 σ_2, all positive); the two conventions yield symbolically different χ^λ values.  The leaf value at q_0 here is anchored against TR_M_AT_Q0, which markov_trace_symbolic computes via the canonical convention; reconciling the assembly chain's symbolic chi steps with the canonical convention is open frontier.
